payload.title: Thinking
payload.text:
I'm setting up three subagents to run in parallel, one for each file, and holding off on running anything myself until they finish. Once they're done I'll run npm test and reply in one line. The subagent prompts have to stand alone, so I'm working out how to brief them on the project location and context.

Still deciding what the subagents may do: they can read the test file and the file they own, and running the single test file is fine as long as they edit nothing but their own file. I'm leaning toward telling them they can run tests read-only, with no edits outside their file.

payload.prompt:
You are fixing one bug in a node/TypeScript project at /private/tmp/vcmp/w/t2 (same as /tmp/vcmp/w/t2). `npm test` runs node:test. Three tests currently fail, and there is exactly one bug in each of src/pricing.ts, src/inventory.ts and src/checkout.ts. Other agents are fixing the other two files in parallel.

Your scope: fix ONLY src/pricing.ts. Do not edit the tests or any other file. You may read anything in the project (the tests, the doc comments, other source files) to understand the expected behaviour. The doc comments in src/pricing.ts describe what the code should do, so use them as the spec.

Steps: read src/pricing.ts and the relevant test file(s) that exercise it, find the single bug, make the minimal fix in src/pricing.ts, and optionally run only the relevant test to confirm (do not edit anything to make it pass). When finished, reply with a short report: the bug you found, the line(s) you changed, and whether the relevant test now passes.

payload.result:
The bug was in `checkout()` in `src/checkout.ts`: when `reserve()` failed for a SKU, the loop silently skipped it with `continue` instead of throwing. The doc comment says it should throw `'out of stock <sku>'`.

**Change (line 6):**
- Before: `if (!reserve(sku, qty)) { continue; }`
- After: `if (!reserve(sku, qty)) { throw new Error(\`out of stock ${sku}\`); }`

**Result:** `test/checkout.test.ts` passes, 2 of 2. That includes "checkout throws when out of stock", which had been failing. I did not touch any other file and did not look at `inventory.ts` or `pricing.ts` beyond what the tests exercise.

The bug was in `reserve()` in `src/inventory.ts`: the guard `if (have <= qty)` refused any reservation that would take the last units, even though the doc comment says it should "take qty units if that many are left."

`test/inventory.test.ts` now passes both of its tests (`inStock` and `reserve can take the last units`). I did not touch any other file.
